summary:
`index.html` is ready in the current folder. It's a 10-second strawberry latte ad drawn on a single canvas. I rendered frames at 8 points in the 10 seconds in headless Chrome and the scenes and text look as intended. I didn't check that two renders of the same time produce identical pixels. Every random value comes from a fixed seed and is set once at load, so they should.

**Storyboard**
| Time | Scene |
|---|---|
| 0–2s | Strawberries fall on a pink background. The "NEW" badge pops in, then "봄을 담은 새로운 한 잔". |
| 2–5.6s | A circle wipe switches to a cream background and a glass rises up. Strawberry purée pours in first ("생딸기 퓨레" label), then milk ("+ 고소한 우유") with pink swirling where they meet. Ice cubes, a striped straw and a strawberry garnish on the rim follow. |
| 5.6–8s | The glass slides left with sparkles. "딸기라떼" pops in one character at a time, then "STRAWBERRY LATTE" and a two-line description. |
| 8–10s | A pink circle wipe brings in the end card: "봄 시즌 한정 출시", the "4,800원" price badge, "지금 가까운 매장에서 만나보세요", the "Café Bloom" logo and confetti. |
| 9.55–10s | It fades back to the opening pink, so the loop from 10s to 0s is seamless. |

**How it meets the submission rules**
- It uses `<canvas id="c">` at 1280×720 and loads no external images, fonts, CDNs or network resources. Text uses fonts already on the system, such as Apple SD Gothic Neo, Malgun Gothic or Noto Sans KR.
- `window.renderFrame(t)` draws the frame for any `t` from 0 to 10 seconds. It doesn't depend on the previous frame.
- Opened in a browser, it repeats every 10 seconds using `requestAnimationFrame`, with no sound.

The price (4,800원) and the café name ("Café Bloom") are placeholders I made up. Change them to your real ones in the `endScene` function.
